patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch is a narrow single-column layout with long stacked content and no visible persistent full navigation; this strongly implies a collapsed mobile navigation control rather than always-visible desktop-style nav.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A hamburger trigger should open and close a mobile navigation panel or overlay containing the site links. The trigger state should toggle between expanded/collapsed and likely lock background scroll while open.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly draw the hamburger icon or the opened menu state, so the exact presentation (drawer, full-screen overlay, dropdown sheet) is unclear.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches depict long vertically scrollable pages with repeated content blocks and substantial page depth, which commonly implies a return-to-top affordance for usability on long galleries/content pages.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A back-to-top control would appear after the user scrolls down and smoothly return focus/scroll position to the top when activated.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit button is drawn in either sketch, so this is inferred from page length rather than directly shown.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly content-driven responsive page with relatively light JavaScript needs. The clearest cross-viewport difference is navigation: desktop appears to have room for persistent navigation or sidebar structure, while mobile likely collapses navigation into a hamburger-controlled panel. Beyond that, the layouts read as largely static content blocks without explicit evidence of tabs, accordions, forms, modals, dropdowns, or dynamic loading. Any scroll-to-top behavior is only weakly inferred from the unusually long page length rather than directly depicted.
